title: Block A close: the long surahs
hook: law, story, battle and mercy woven together, and every surah but one opening with mercy

segments.voice: Yesterday: hasbiya Allah, the last verse of at-Tawbah, and your line, allah is enough. Today is the last day of Block A.

Ninety-five days ago, this year began with seven verses said seventeen times a day. Since then you've walked through the long surahs at the front of the Qur'an, most of them revealed in Medina, where a small community became a city with neighbors, treaties, marriages, markets and wars. A reader expecting nothing but prayer finds something else. Inheritance shares sit beside the Throne verse. A debt contract sits beside a prayer for strength. A battle sits beside a verse about a single heart. And nearly every one of those surahs opens the same way.

Here's Block A in nine doors. Al-Fatiha: a conversation, praise and then asking. Al-Baqarah: the cow, the Throne verse, no compulsion in religion, write your debts down, and a God who burdens no soul beyond what it can bear. Al 'Imran: Maryam, chosen above the women of the worlds, a common word with the People of the Book, and the Prophet's gentleness: had you been harsh, they would have scattered. An-Nisa: live with them in kindness, stand for justice even against yourselves, greet with something better. Al-Ma'idah: whoever saves one life, it is as if he saved all humanity; compete in good; the table from heaven. Al-An'am: not a leaf falls without His knowing; don't insult the gods of others. Al-A'raf: am I not your Lord, asked before we were born, and the garment of piety. Al-Anfal: if they incline to peace, incline to it too. At-Tawbah: the cave, the three left behind, and enough for me. Law, story, battle, and running through all of it, mercy. Now count the openings. Of the Qur'an's one hundred fourteen surahs, every one opens with bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim, in the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind, except at-Tawbah. And, as you saw a week ago, the missing bismillah turns up inside another surah, an-Naml, in a letter from Sulayman, so the phrase still appears one hundred fourteen times. Before every law, story and battle in these pages, the reader passes through those words. However hard the room, mercy was the door you came in by.
screen: `A CONVERSATION; THE THRONE VERSE.` · `MARYAM; JUSTICE; ONE LIFE.` · `NOT A LEAF; AM I NOT YOUR LORD?` · `PEACE; THE CAVE; ENOUGH FOR ME.` · then, large: `MERCY WAS ALWAYS THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Let the nine doors pass by slowly, one per breath or two: the Fatiha, the Cow, the Family of 'Imran, the Women, the Table, the Cattle, the Heights, the Spoils, the Repentance. At each one, let a single line or picture come back, whatever stayed with you. If you pray, you can begin with bismillah.
Bismillah, in the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind. The door that opens every surah but one, appearing one hundred fourteen times in all. Today's word.
Your line: mercy was always the door. Tomorrow Block B begins: prophets, parables and light, starting with Surah Yunus. Block A, complete.

howItsDone: Muslims begin the recitation of every surah except at-Tawbah with bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim, and many who read the Qur'an through mark the end of the long opening surahs as a milestone in their reading.

chat.says: Why does almost every surah start with bismillah?
options: Every surah but one opens with it, so the reader passes through mercy first.
It's a prayer for protection, said only before the hardest surahs.
It's said only before the Medinan surahs, the ones that contain law.
chat.meaning: Of the 114 surahs, every one opens with bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim except at-Tawbah. Before every law, story and battle, mercy is the door.
